verdict.reasoning: Doctor summarizes: "last three days, you've been having bit of burning pain on passing urine" and patient earlier describes it as a "stinging kind of pain" when she pees.

Patient: "it's sort of like a stinging kind of pain... when I pee" and "I also maybe sometimes get some like, pain kind of lower down in my tummy, when I, when I go to the bathroom"; she later describes it as "sort of cramping."
Patient: "there was a little bit of blood earlier today" and "It does kind of... doesn't smell very, it smells a bit weird." This supports small amount of hematuria and malodorous urine.

Patient denies frequency ("not, I don't think so"), flank/back pain ("Does the pain move... towards your flank?" Patient: "No, not really"), nausea/vomiting ("Uh, no, not at all"), fever ("No, no, no fever, no"), and diarrhea ("Uh, no, not that I've noticed at all").
Patient: "in the past I've had some uh, some IBS."
Doctor: "Do you take any regular medications?" Patient: "Uh, no" then only mentions trying OTC bicarbonate, indicating no regular meds.
Patient: "I did... a couple of days ago, try some uh, over the counter bicarbonate, to try and help with the pain but it wasn't really helping."
Patient: "I'm allergic to, Clindamycin" and when asked what happens: "I get some like a, a, a swelling, basically."
Doctor asks about family history "related to kidneys, bladder, bowels, guts?" Patient: "Uh, no I don't think so, not that I, not anything I know about."
Patient: "I live in a flat near my college, with a couple of like friends of mine"; "I'm a student" studying biology; "I don't smoke, I do drink, like on the weekends."
Patient: "yeah I am" sexually active; has "a boyfriend for about a, a couple of months now"; uses contraception: "yeah, we use condoms."
STI screen: Patient: "Don't think I've ever, I don't think I've ever had one." Pregnancy: Patient says "I don't think so" when asked if she could be pregnant, matching "unlikely to be pregnant."
Doctor: "And when was your last, period?" Patient: "Uh, couple of weeks ago." Doctor clarifies: "Three weeks ago, OK." This supports approximately 3 weeks.
Doctor: "I think probably do have what we call a simple UTI or urinary tract infection, bladder infection." This is equivalent to acute uncomplicated cystitis.
Allergy to Clindamycin with swelling is documented, supporting this being an active drug allergy.
Doctor: "I'll give you a course of antibiotics today. Something, called either Nitrofurantoin, or Trimethoprim. And it's normally a three day course. So, one tablet, twice a day, for three days."
Doctor: "I also advise you to drink plenty of fluids... You can try, cranberry juice, that can sometimes help with your symptoms."

Doctor: "if you can try and avoid [sex], I think that'd be sensible... it's great that you're using barrier contraception. I would recommend you to continue using barrier contraception, but if you can avoid it while your symptoms clear up."

Doctor: "if you're still not better, by the end of this week, I want you to give me a call" and "things to look out for would be... high temperatures, a back pain, just generally feeling more unwell... do give me a call if you're having any concerns."
Doctor: "if... you are worried about the pain... then I'd always advise getting a pregnancy test, to rule out pregnancy." This corresponds to taking a test if there is concern.
There is discussion that she has never had an STD screen, but no plan is stated to arrange the first STI screen.
Although a Clindamycin allergy is recorded, the doctor does not explicitly advise to avoid Clindamycin in the future.
